401090229c631e53.title: Sokencool Tablet
401090229c631e53.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for indigestion, loss of appetite (poor appetite), overeating, food stagnation, promotion of digestion, and upper abdominal bloating caused by indigestion.
401090229c631e53.usage:
Adults and those aged 15 and over take 2 tablets at a time, 3 times a day after meals.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
401090229c631e53.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: children aged 7 or under, patients hypersensitive to soybean oil or with a history of allergic reactions to it, patients hypersensitive to soybeans or peanuts, or patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a lipid metabolism disorder such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, or pancreatitis, have an allergic constitution, or are at particular risk from fat overload.

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

Consult a pharmacist when taking together with lipid emulsions or other intravenous lipid preparations.

If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

4da3b7a0f97b4206.title: Calsumer Tablet
4da3b7a0f97b4206.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamin D during pregnancy and breastfeeding, growth periods, and in old age, to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets, and to supply calcium for calcium deficiency and other calcium needs.
4da3b7a0f97b4206.usage:
Adults and those aged 8 and over take 2 tablets once a day after meals.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
4da3b7a0f97b4206.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients hypersensitive to this medicine, or patients with hypercalcemia, sarcoidosis, kidney disease, kidney stones, or severe renal failure, or infants under 12 months of age.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or possibly pregnant or breastfeeding, in the case of premature or young infants, or if you have cardiac or circulatory dysfunction, kidney impairment, or hypoproteinemia, are taking cardiac glycosides, or have had kidney stones.

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, or antacids. Use caution when taking together with anti-aldosterone agents or triamterene, as this may cause hyperkalemia. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If you experience nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, or skin rash, or if symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Adults and those aged 8 and over take 2 capsules once a day after meals.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
69d379dfe5e8d7f4.caution:
Warning: Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A per day may cause congenital malformations. Do not take this medicine if you are within the first 3 months of pregnancy or possibly pregnant. Overdose in children aged 6 or under may cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep out of reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients hypersensitive to this medicine or to soybean oil, soybeans, or peanuts, patients with hypercalcemia (excess calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause), or kidney disease, infants under 12 months of age, or patients with Wilson's disease, hemochromatosis (a disease in which iron deposits in the liver and pancreas due to abnormal iron metabolism), hemosiderosis, non-iron-deficiency anemia, kidney stones, or severe renal failure.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hyperoxaluria (a condition in which excessive oxalate is excreted in the urine), are pregnant or possibly pregnant or breastfeeding, in the case of premature or young infants, or if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional colitis, cardiac or circulatory dysfunction, kidney impairment, hypoproteinemia, gallbladder-related disease, liver disease, or gout, have had kidney stones, are deficient in folic acid, or have a predisposition to thrombosis (blood vessel blockage).

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

This medicine may interfere with the detection of blood sugar in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, affecting clinical test values.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids, or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist when taking together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen, anti-aldosterone agents, triamterene, or cardiac glycosides. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If you experience nausea, vomiting, itching, dry rough skin, painful joint swelling, diarrhea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, redness (flushing), loose stools, stomatitis (sores in the mouth), loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, skin rash, hives, photosensitivity, abdominal or stomach pain, cramps, fever, drowsiness, upper abdominal pain, dermatitis, odor in sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, pulmonary edema, or if menstruation starts earlier than expected, becomes gradually heavier, or bleeding lasts longer, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.
